symbols.name: qK
symbols.def: \(q_{P^{(n)},K}(u)\) is the smallest center in \(C_{P^{(n)},K}\) attaining \(\min_{c\in C_{P^{(n)},K}}|u-c|\).

symbols.name: ZP
symbols.def: \((Z_{P^{(n)},K}:1\le K<K_n)\) is centered Gaussian with covariance \(R_{P^{(n)}}\).

symbols.name: hatGK
symbols.def: \(\widehat G_K=\widehat\rho(K+1)-\widehat\rho(K)\), where every \(\widehat W_K\) is a cross-fitted corrected loss minimized over \(\mathcal C_K\), every inverse propensity uses \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\), \(\widehat\rho(K)=1-\widehat W_K/\widehat W_1\), and every nonunique empirical minimizer is resolved by the deterministic measurable rule selecting the lexicographically smallest ordered codebook.

symbols.name: tildepsiK
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\psi_{i,K}\) is the uncentered cross-fitted plug-in value for \(\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}(O_{n,i})\), evaluated with the nuisance fits and deterministic empirical codebook selectors trained outside the fold containing unit \(i\), and with \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\) in every inverse weight.

symbols.name: hatsigmaK
symbols.def: \(\widehat\sigma_K^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K})^2\) and \(\widehat\sigma_K=\{\widehat\sigma_K^2\}^{1/2}\) is the nonnegative square root.

symbols.name: xi
symbols.def: Conditionally on the data, \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\) and are independent of the data.

symbols.name: qalpha
symbols.def: Let \(T_n^{\#}=\max_{1\le K<K_n:\widehat\sigma_K>0}|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\widehat\sigma_K|\), with the maximum over the empty set defined as zero. Then \(q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:P(T_n^{\#}\le t\mid O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n})\ge1-\alpha\}\).

symbols.name: IK
symbols.def: If \(\widehat\sigma_K>0\), then \(I_{n,K}=[\widehat G_K-q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K/\sqrt n,\widehat G_K+q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K/\sqrt n]\); if \(\widehat\sigma_K=0\), set \(I_{n,K}=\mathbb R\).

symbols.name: Bsharp
symbols.def: \(B_n^{\#}=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}I_{n,K}\) is the single data-measurable band produced by the corrected estimator and multiplier quantile.

symbols.name: PU
symbols.def:
Under \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\), \(X=U\), \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of \(U\), \(Y(1)=U-1/2+
u_n\varepsilon_1\), and \(Y(0)=1/2-U+
u_n\varepsilon_0\), with independent Rademacher marks \(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1\).

symbols.name: Bp
symbols.def: \(B_1(t)=t-1/2\) and \(B_2(t)=t^2-t+1/6\) for \(t\in[0,1)\), extended with period one.

symbols.name: cfano
symbols.def: \(c_{\mathrm F}>0\) is fixed and sufficiently small.

symbols.name: Ptilt
symbols.def:
For \(j\in J_n\),
\[
 \frac{dP_j^{(n)}}{dP_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(o)\}}
 {\mathbb E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(O)\}]},
\]
and \(P_0^{(n)}=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: Un
symbols.def: \(\mathcal U_n=\{P_0^{(n)}\}\cup\{P_j^{(n)}:j\in J_n\}\), with the laws supplied by \(Ptilt\).

symbols.name: Vband
symbols.def: \(V_n\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) is independent of the sample under every row law; a procedure that does not randomize ignores this argument.

symbols.name: bandLower
symbols.def: \(L_{n,K}=L_{n,K}(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)\) is measurable and does not depend on \(P^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: bandUpper
symbols.def: \(U_{n,K}=U_{n,K}(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)\) is measurable, does not depend on \(P^{(n)}\), and satisfies \(L_{n,K}\le U_{n,K}\).

symbols.name: Bband
symbols.def: \(B_n(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\) is one common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable map.

symbols.name: bandHalf
symbols.def: \(h_{n,K}=(U_{n,K}-L_{n,K})/2\), with \(h_{n,K}=+\infty\) when an endpoint is infinite.

symbols.name: HonestBand
symbols.type: uniform-honesty predicate over the local experiment
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\) holds when there exists a deterministic sequence \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) such that \[\inf_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\{G_{P^{(n)}}(K)\in[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\text{ for every }1\le K<K_n\}\ge1-\alpha-\eta_n.\] The probability integrates the declared auxiliary randomization.

symbols.name: Pgeo
symbols.def:
For \(j\in J_n\), \(dP_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)}/dP_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}=\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma_j^{\mathrm g}(U)\}/\mathbb E_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma_j^{\mathrm g}(U)\}]\), and \(P_{0,\mathrm g}^{(n)}=P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: Pres
symbols.def:
For \(j\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}\), \(dP_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)}/dP_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}=\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm h}\}/\mathbb E_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm h}\}]\), and \(P_{0,\mathrm r}^{(n)}=P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: Unstar
symbols.def: \(\mathcal U_n^\star=\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm g}\) if \(\nu_nK_n\leq1\), and \(\mathcal U_n^\star=\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm r}\) if \(\nu_nK_n>1\).

assumptions.condition: \(\epsilon\le e_{P^{(n)}}(X)\le1-\epsilon\) almost surely for a fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\).

novel.justification: The normalization fixes a common interpretable scale for customer-level causal contrasts and is satisfied after rescaling any application with a known bounded contrast range, including binary outcomes and the uniform randomized-trial witness.

assumptions.condition: For every \(1\le K\le K_n\), \(C_{P^{(n)},K}\) is a singleton \((c_{P^{(n)},K,1},\ldots,c_{P^{(n)},K,K})\) satisfying \(0<c_{P^{(n)},K,1}<\cdots<c_{P^{(n)},K,K}<1\).

novel.justification: Unique interior population segmentations are stable for scalar feature laws with densities bounded above and below near the uniform law; the condition rules out scientifically ambiguous tied segmentations while allowing cell widths and curvature to deteriorate with resolution.

assumptions.condition: For every \(K\le K_n\) and every ordered codebook \(C\in\mathcal C_K\) with \(\min_{\pi}\|C-\pi C_{P^{(n)},K}\|_2\le\kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\), its excess distortion is at least \(\lambda_{P^{(n)},K}\min_{\pi}\|C-\pi C_{P^{(n)},K}\|_2^2\).

novel.justification: A local quadratic-growth modulus is the nonsmooth formulation of optimizer stability needed for increasing resolution; it holds for densities bounded away from zero around the uniform law and does not presume twice differentiability of the distortion.

assumptions.condition: For every \(K\le K_n\) and \(0<t\le\kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\), \(P^{(n)}[\operatorname{dist}\{b_{P^{(n)}}(X),\mathcal B_{P^{(n)},K}\}\le t s_{P^{(n)},K}]\le M_{P^{(n)},K}t^{\alpha_{P^{(n)},K}}\).

novel.justification: This resolution-indexed version of the quantization margin condition retains the shrinking cell radius and is satisfied uniformly by scalar densities bounded near the uniform density; Levrard's fixed-resolution margin condition is its geometric antecedent.

assumptions.condition: The primitive functions \(e_{P^{(n)}},\mu_{0,P^{(n)}},\mu_{1,P^{(n)}}\) admit cross-fitted estimators whose maximum \(L_2(P_X^{(n)})\) error, with uniform error for the two outcome regressions, is \(O_{P^{(n)}}(r_n)\) uniformly over the row class.

novel.justification: The lower bound isolates a nonvanishing causal-heterogeneity regime in which the ratio profile is uniformly defined; it is satisfied by the uniform witness, for which \(W(1)=1/12\), and excludes drift to a homogeneous-effect law.

Positive adjacent-score variance is the minimal coordinatewise condition for studentizing resolution gains; the exact witness calculation verifies it while allowing the raw variances to shrink at resolution-dependent rates.

definitions.name: triangular causal-quantizer class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}=\{P^{(n)}:P^{(n)}\text{ satisfies ass:consistency, ass:exchangeability, ass:overlap, ass:bounded-feature, ass:unique-interior-codebooks, ass:quadratic-growth, ass:growing-margin, ass:nuisance-estimability, ass:resolution-denominator, and ass:score-nondegeneracy for row }n\}\).

definitions.name: corrected growing-resolution profile
definitions.construction: On each validation fold, clip the fitted propensity to \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\), insert it and the fitted outcome regressions into the corrected loss induced by \(\phi_{W,P^{(n)},K}\), minimize the empirical corrected loss over \(\mathcal C_K\) for every \(1\le K\le K_n\), select the lexicographically smallest ordered minimizer, and form \(\widehat G_K\), the raw foldwise values \(\widetilde\psi_{i,K}\), their mean \(\overline\psi_K\), the centered values \(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}\), and the nonnegative \(\widehat\sigma_K\) as declared in the symbol table.

definitions.name: common measurable rectangular band
definitions.construction: Fix one sequence of \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable maps \(B_n=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\) with \(L_{n,K}\le U_{n,K}\), coordinate half-widths \(h_{n,K}=(U_{n,K}-L_{n,K})/2\), and only the declared independent \(V_n\) as optional auxiliary randomization. Uniform honesty over \(\mathcal U_n\) means \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\) as declared in the symbol table.

definitions.name: covariance-aware multiplier band
definitions.construction: Compute \(q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\) as the conditional quantile infimum of the joint multiplier maximum over exactly the coordinates with \(\widehat\sigma_K>0\), retaining the empirical cross-resolution covariance, and report \(\{I_{n,K}:1\le K<K_n\}\), with \(I_{n,K}=\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat\sigma_K=0\). This is a single common measurable rectangular-band procedure and uses neither oracle \(P^{(n)}\)-indexed endpoints nor independent-coordinate calibration.

definitions.name: multi-resolution Fano family
definitions.construction:
Use the base law and all inward-oriented one-hot score tilts \(\{P_j^{(n)}:j\in J_n\}\), with
\[
 \frac{dP_j^{(n)}}{dP_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(o)\}}
 {\mathbb E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(O)\}]},
\]
and \(P_0^{(n)}=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\).  Each likelihood is normalized separately.  The negative orientation is required before imposing a quantitative growing-resolution support-and-quantizer-stability regime; it points the first-order outcome-regression displacement inward at both endpoints.

definitions.name: warped Bernoulli-score handle
definitions.construction: Start from the probability-integral transform of the causal-feature law, expand optimized residual and loss contrasts in the transported periodic Bernoulli basis, and orthogonalize the resulting score directions against the nuisance tangent space to target the observational cross-resolution kernel.

definitions.name: positive-noise geometric Fano family
definitions.construction:
For \(K\geq1\), set
\[
 F^{\mathrm g}_K(u)=\sum_{a\in\{1,K,K+1\}}w_{K,2}(a)B_2(au),\qquad
 \gamma^{\mathrm g}_K(u)=\frac{12F^{\mathrm g}_K(u)}{\sqrt{V_K^{(0)}}}.
\]
For every \(j\in J_n\), define the \(U\)-only geometric tilt by
\[
 \frac{dP_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)}}{dP_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma^{\mathrm g}_j(u)\}}
 {\mathbb E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma^{\mathrm g}_j(U)\}]},
\]
put \(P_{0,\mathrm g}^{(n)}=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\), and set
\(\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm g}=\{P_{0,\mathrm g}^{(n)}\}\cup\{P_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)}:j\in J_n\}\).  Each likelihood is normalized separately and changes only the marginal law of \(U=X\); its negative orientation is the same inward orientation as the noiseless family.

definitions.name: hybrid residual-score Fano family
definitions.construction:
Fix \(a_{\mathrm h}\in(0,1/16]\).  On every row with \(\nu_n>0\), use the high-resolution labels \(J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}\), the normalized residual direction \(\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm r}\), and the hybrid inward score \(\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm h}=\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm r}+a_{\mathrm h}\gamma_j^{\mathrm g}(U)\).  For \(j\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}\), define
\[
 \frac{dP_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)}}{dP_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm h}(o)\}}
 {\mathbb E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm h}(O)\}]},
\]
put \(P_{0,\mathrm r}^{(n)}=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\), and set \(\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm r}=\{P_{0,\mathrm r}^{(n)}\}\cup\{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)}:j\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}\}\).  The fixed geometric component reinforces the denominator at its equality boundary; the residual component supplies the high-noise separation.

definitions.name: piecewise all-noise Fano experiment
definitions.construction:
Define the rowwise branch
\[
 (\mathcal U_n^\star,I_n^\star)=
 \begin{cases}
 (\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm g},J_n),&\nu_nK_n\leq1,\\
 (\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm r},J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}),&\nu_nK_n>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus the low-noise rows use the geometric packing and the high-noise rows use the hybrid residual packing; the definition makes no upper-band claim.

statements.statement:
For every row \(n\), every \(0\leq
u_n\leq1/4\), and every \(K\leq K_n\), provided the fixed denominator constant satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\), the law \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\) satisfies the causal, support, unique-interior-codebook, local quadratic-growth, growing-margin, denominator, and score-nondegeneracy conditions of \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\). Its unique centers are \(c_{K,j}=(2j-1)/(2K)\), its boundaries are \(j/K\), and \(W_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K)=1/(12K^2)\).
statements.justification: This establishes a nonempty bounded causal experiment in which every geometric and inferential quantity is explicit.
statements.gap: Pollard1982Central and Levrard2015 analyze observed fixed-resolution quantizers, while KimKimKennedy2026 does not give a growing-resolution causal witness.
statements.consumer: MineThatData analysts obtain a calibrated benchmark for how many customer-effect segments can be distinguished under randomized-treatment noise.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(P=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\) and fix the row \(n\).  The witness construction and the mean-zero Rademacher marks give
\[
 e_P(u)=\tfrac12,\qquad
 \mu_{1,P}(u)=u-\tfrac12,\qquad
 \mu_{0,P}(u)=\tfrac12-u .
\]
Consistency holds by construction.  Since \(A\) is independent of \((U,\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1)\), conditional exchangeability holds.  The overlap inequalities follow from \(\epsilon<1/2=e_P(u)<1-\epsilon\).  Moreover,
\[
 b_P(u)=\{\mu_{1,P}(u)-\mu_{0,P}(u)+1\}/2=u,
 \qquad |\mu_{1,P}(u)-\mu_{0,P}(u)|=|2u-1|\leq1.
\]
Since \(0\leq u\leq1\) and \(0\leq\nu_n\leq1/4\), both potential outcomes, and hence \(Y\), lie in \([-3/4,3/4]\subset[-1,1]\).  The three nuisance functions displayed above are common known functions throughout the witness family, so the data-independent fits equal to those functions have error zero, which is \(O_P(r_n)\).  This proves the causal, support, and nuisance-estimability conditions.

Any ordered scalar codebook induces at most \(K\) interval cells.  Let their lengths, including zeros for empty cells, be \(p_1,\ldots,p_K\), where \(p_j\geq0\) and \(\sum_jp_j=1\).  For an interval of length \(p\), completion of the square gives
\[
 \inf_c\int_a^{a+p}(u-c)^2\,du
 =\int_a^{a+p}\left(u-a-\frac p2\right)^2du
 =\frac{p^3}{12},
\]
and the minimizer is unique when \(p>0\).  Therefore Jensen's inequality, with strictness unless all cell lengths agree, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\min_{c\in C}(U-c)^2
 \geq \frac1{12}\sum_{j=1}^Kp_j^3
 \geq\frac1{12K^2}.
\]
Equality requires \(p_j=1/K\) for every \(j\) and each center to be its cell midpoint.  Consequently
\[
 c_{K,j}=\frac{2j-1}{2K},\qquad
 \mathcal B_{P,K}=\left\{\frac jK:1\leq j<K\right\},
 \qquad W_P(K)=\frac1{12K^2}.
\]
The centers are uniquely strictly ordered and interior.  Also \(W_P(1)=1/12\), so the denominator condition holds precisely under the stated qualification \(\underline w\leq1/12\).

Near the displayed codebook, differentiation under the cell integrals is valid because the losses of adjacent centers agree at each moving Voronoi boundary.  At the optimum, for \(K\geq2\), the Hessian is
\[
 H_K=\frac1{2K}
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3&-1&0&\cdots&0\\
 -1&2&-1&\ddots&\vdots\\
 0&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\
 \vdots&\ddots&-1&2&-1\\
 0&\cdots&0&-1&3
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(x\in\mathbb R^K\),
\[
 2Kx^{\mathsf T}H_Kx
 =\sum_{j=1}^{K-1}(x_{j+1}-x_j)^2+2x_1^2+2x_K^2>0
\]
unless \(x=0\); for \(K=1\), the second derivative is \(2\).  Hessian continuity therefore supplies positive \(\kappa_{P,K}\) and \(\lambda_{P,K}\) for which the required quadratic-growth inequality holds.  Because both codebooks are ordered, the rearrangement inequality makes the identity permutation minimize the permutation distance.

The maximum cell radius is \(s_{P,K}=1/(2K)\).  Choose the preceding validity radius no larger than one.  For \(0<t\leq\kappa_{P,K}\), the intervals of radius \(t/(2K)\) around the \(K-1\) boundaries are disjoint up to endpoints, and hence
\[
 P\{\operatorname{dist}(U,\mathcal B_{P,K})\leq ts_{P,K}\}
 =(K-1)t/K\leq t.
\]
Thus the margin condition holds with \(\alpha_{P,K}=1\) and \(M_{P,K}=1\).

Finally,
\[
 \zeta_P(O)=\nu_n\{A\varepsilon_1-(1-A)\varepsilon_0\},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P(\zeta_P\mid U)=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P(\zeta_P^2\mid U)=\nu_n^2.
\]
Outside the null set of cell boundaries, the periodic Bernoulli-polynomial identities are
\[
 U-q_{P,a}(U)=a^{-1}B_1(aU),\qquad
 \ell_{P,a}(U)=a^{-2}\{B_2(aU)+1/12\}.
\]
Substitution into the influence functions gives
\[
 \Delta\phi_{P,K}
 =12\sum_aw_{K,2}(a)B_2(aU)
 +24\zeta_P\sum_aw_{K,1}(a)B_1(aU),
\]
where each sum is over \(\{1,K,K+1\}\).  The two summands are uncorrelated by the conditional mean-zero identity.  Partitioning \([0,1]\) at the common grid with mesh \(1/\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), expanding the two polynomial pieces, and summing the resulting finite power sums gives
\[
 \int_0^1B_2(au)B_2(bu)\,du=\frac{\gcd(a,b)^4}{180a^2b^2}.
\]
The diagonal geometric contribution is therefore
\[
 \frac{8N_K}{5K^6(K+1)^6},\qquad
 N_K=K^8+4K^7+10K^6+16K^5+5K^4-12K^3-14K^2-6K-1.
\]
For \(x=K-1\geq0\), direct expansion yields
\[
 N_K=x^8+12x^7+66x^6+216x^5+445x^4+564x^3+402x^2+126x+3>0.
\]
Thus \(\sigma_{P,K}>0\) for every adjacent coordinate, including when \(\nu_n=0\).  All declared conditions follow.

statements.statement:
Under \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\), the complete adjacent-score covariance is \[\Sigma_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)=144H_2(K,L)+576
u_n^2H_1(K,L).\] In particular, \(\sigma_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)},K}^2=V_K^{(0)}+
u_n^2A_K\). The arithmetic kernel implies \[\sup_{\substack{K
e L\,;\ K,L\ge8}}R_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\le0.28,\qquad d_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\ge1.2,\] uniformly over \(
u_n\in[0,1/4]\). Thus \(J_n\) is a covariance-separated packing with \(|J_n|=(K_n-8)_+\), and universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) satisfy \[c\sqrt{\log(2+K_n)}\le w_n(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)})\le C\sqrt{\log(2+K_n)}.\]
statements.justification: The full covariance, rather than the diagonal variance or coordinate count, determines the simultaneous resolution penalty.
statements.gap: KimKimKennedy2026 supplies fixed-resolution influence functions and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2017 supplies generic Gaussian approximation, but neither computes this arithmetic covariance kernel or its diverging packing.
statements.consumer: The covariance formula lets a MineThatData analysis replace conservative independent-coordinate calibration by the actual joint resolution geometry.

statements.statement:
Set \(\nu_n=0\) in \(\mathcal U_n\), and suppose the fixed class denominator satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\).  In \(\texttt{def:corrected-profile-estimator}\), use a fixed finite number of deterministic folds whose training sizes are at least a fixed positive fraction of \(n\), and use the common known nuisance functions \(e(u)=1/2\), \(\mu_1(u)=u-1/2\), and \(\mu_0(u)=1/2-u\), so that \(r_n=0\).  If \(\delta_nK_n^3\to0\) and \(K_n^5L_n\to0\), then, uniformly over \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n\), every empirical codebook selected by the estimator enters its population quadratic-growth basin and has ordered Euclidean displacement \(O_{P^{(n)}}(\delta^C_{P^{(n)},K,n})\), simultaneously over \(K\leq K_n\).  Moreover,
\[
 \max_{1\leq K<K_n}\frac{|\widehat G_K-G_{P^{(n)}}(K)-(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P^{(n)})\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}|}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 =O_{P^{(n)}}\!\left(\max_{K<K_n}\frac{R^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}\right),
\]
and the maximum coordinatewise \(L_2(P^{(n)})\) discrepancy between \(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\) and \(\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}(O_{n,i})/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\) is
\[
 O_{P^{(n)}}\!\left(\max_{K<K_n}\frac{S^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}\right).
\]
If additionally \(\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P^{(n)})\to0\), then
\[
 \max_{1\leq K<K_n}\left|\frac{\widehat\sigma_K}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}-1\right|=o_{P^{(n)}}(1)
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal U_n\), \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\) with probability tending to one uniformly, and all reoptimization, score-estimation, and variance-estimation effects on the studentized maximum are negligible on the intrinsic Gaussian-width scale.
statements.justification: The theorem derives empirical basin entry and corrected reoptimization control on the specified noiseless experiment while separating the \(K_n^5L_n\) empirical requirement from the sharper \(\delta_nK_n^3\) membership requirement.
statements.gap: The fixed- or level-by-level quantizer results in Pollard1982Central, Levrard2015, and LiuPages2020 do not supply simultaneous shrinking-score linearization for a corrected causal profile.
statements.consumer: The derived remainder comparison tells MineThatData analysts whether codebook fitting reaches the local basin before joint uncertainty dominates.

statements.statement:
Let \(\nu_n=0\), suppose the fixed class denominator satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\), suppose \(|J_n|\geq2\) eventually, and suppose \(\delta_nK_n^3\to0\).  Then every likelihood in \(\texttt{def:fano-family}\) is normalized and has the same support, treatment mechanism, conditional outcome laws, causal feature \(b(u)=u\), and oracle nuisance functions as \(P_0^{(n)}=P_{U,0}^{(n)}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), every \(P_j^{(n)}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\), with constants uniform in \(j\in J_n\): its feature density \(f_{n,j}\) satisfies \(\|f_{n,j}-1\|_\infty\leq C\delta_n\); its population codebooks are unique and obey
\[
 \|C_{P_j^{(n)},K}-C_{P_0^{(n)},K}\|_2\leq C\delta_nK^{3/2},\quad
 \lambda_{P_j^{(n)},K}\geq cK^{-3},\quad
 s_{P_j^{(n)},K}\asymp K^{-1},
\]
and one may take \(\kappa_{P_j^{(n)},K}=c/K\), \(\alpha_{P_j^{(n)},K}=1\), and \(M_{P_j^{(n)},K}\leq C\), uniformly over \(1\leq K\leq K_n\).  Moreover,
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}\left|\frac{\sigma_{P_j^{(n)},K}}{\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}}-1\right|
 +\sup_{K,L<K_n}|R_{P_j^{(n)}}(K,L)-R_{P_0^{(n)}}(K,L)|
 \leq C\delta_nK_n^2=o(1),
\]
and, uniformly over \(K<K_n\),
\[
 G_{P_j^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_0^{(n)}}(K)
 =-\delta_n\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}R_{P_0^{(n)}}(K,j)
 +O\!\left(\delta_n^2K_n^2\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}\right).
\]
There is a fixed \(a_0>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \min_{j\ne\ell\,;\ j,\ell\in J_n}\max_{K\in J_n}
 \frac{|G_{P_j^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_\ell^{(n)}}(K)|}{\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}}
 \geq a_0\delta_n,
\]
and \(\operatorname{KL}\{(P_j^{(n)})^{\otimes n},(P_0^{(n)})^{\otimes n}\}\leq Cn\delta_n^2\).
statements.justification: The noiseless inward adjacent-score tilt supplies a genuine within-class multi-resolution experiment through \(\delta_nK_n^3=o(1)\), with standardized covariance and gain remainders of order \(\delta_nK_n^2\).
statements.gap: Levrard2015 gives a fixed-resolution excess-distortion lower-bound construction; it does not certify a growing observed-data causal likelihood packing aligned with adjacent influence scores.
statements.consumer: The result makes failure of fine MineThatData resolution reports information-theoretic on the specified noiseless experiment and supplies the substrate for the separate small-positive-noise converse.

statements.statement:
Set \(\nu_n=0\) in the local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\), and suppose the fixed class denominator satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\).  If \(\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P^{(n)})\to0\), the band in \(\texttt{def:intrinsic-bootstrap-band}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n^{\#},\mathcal U_n)\).  On the event \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\), whose probability tends to one uniformly over this experiment, its simultaneous standardized half-width obeys
\[
 \max_{1\leq K<K_n}\frac{q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 =q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\{1+o_{P^{(n)}}(1)\}
 \asymp_{P^{(n)}}w_n(P^{(n)}).
\]
Conversely, for every sequence of common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable rectangular-band procedures in \(\texttt{def:rectangular-band-procedure}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\), there are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\), depending at most on \(\alpha\) and \(c_{\mathrm F}\) but independent of \(n\) and \(K_n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), some \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\left\{\max_{K\in J_n}\frac{\sqrt n\,h_{n,K}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 \geq c_0\sqrt{\log|J_n|}\right\}\geq c_1.
\]
Consequently the attainable and necessary radii over this noiseless causal experiment have the same intrinsic order
\[
 w_n(P^{(n)})/\sqrt n\asymp\sqrt{\log K_n/n}.
\]
statements.justification: The covariance-aware multiplier upper band and the multi-resolution information bound meet at the same intrinsic width on the explicit bounded-feature-safe causal experiment.
statements.gap: Existing fixed-target causal quantization, fixed-level quantizer geometry, and supplied-score bootstrap results do not jointly prove a matched covariance-aware upper and causal Fano lower radius for the adjacent-resolution process.
statements.consumer: A MineThatData report gains an honest rate-optimal rule for the entire resolution curve in the noiseless benchmark, while noisy matching is not claimed.

Under \(P_{U,

u_n}^{(n)}}(K)=g_K\) and \[\sigma_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)},K}^2=\left\{ rac{8}{5K^4}+ rac{96

u_nK=O(1)\), and \(G(K)/\sigma_K\asymp(
u_nK^2)^{-1}\) when \(
u_nK	o\infty\). For \(K_n=2\), the band reduces to a one-coordinate ratio delta-method interval built from the fixed-risk influence scores.
statements.justification: The reduction rejects a raw-gap heuristic and checks both the noiseless and noisy high-resolution regimes against the fixed-coordinate case.
statements.gap: KimKimKennedy2026 establishes fixed-target asymptotic normality but does not derive the adjacent standardized-gap phase transition.
statements.consumer: The phase transition tells MineThatData users when outcome noise, rather than geometric quantization error, determines the finest reportable segmentation.

statements.statement: Using def:heteroskedastic-extension-handle, characterize the weakest primitive conditions under which a nonuniform causal-feature law with heteroskedastic efficient residual admits an explicit cross-resolution semimetric, a diverging covariance-separated packing, and a corrected band whose upper radius and multi-resolution lower bound both equal its intrinsic Gaussian width. Determine when the width is \(\sqrt{\log K_n}\), \(\sqrt{\log\log K_n}\), or bounded.
statements.justification: The uniform arithmetic kernel is a sharp benchmark, but empirical causal-feature densities can induce qualitatively different dependence across resolutions.
statements.gap: The supplied-score approximation papers do not derive covariance geometry from an optimized causal target, and the causal clustering papers do not classify intrinsic simultaneous complexity.
statements.consumer: An answer would let observational heterogeneous-treatment-effect studies select the correct joint penalty from their estimated feature geometry rather than inherit the uniform benchmark.

statements.statement:
If \((Z_1,\ldots,Z_p)\) is a centered Gaussian vector with unit marginal variances and \(M=\max_{1\leq j\leq p}|Z_j|\), then, for every \(h>0\),
\[
 \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathbb P(|M-t|\leq h)
 \leq Ch\sqrt{\log(2p)},
\]
where \(C\) is numerical and does not depend on \(p\) or the covariance matrix.

source.locator: Appendix A, Gaussian anti-concentration lemma used in the proof of Theorem 2.1
source.verbatim_statement: Lemma A.1 (Nazarov’s inequality). Let Y=(Y_1,...,Y_p) be a centered Gaussian random vector in R^p such that E[Y_j^2] >= b for all j=1,...,p and some constant b>0. Then for every y in R^p and a>0, P(Y <= y+a)-P(Y <= y) <= C a sqrt(log p), where C is a constant depending only on b.

upstream.citation: Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, Central Limit Theorems and Bootstrap in High Dimensions, arXiv:1412.3661v4

attestation.note: Lawful author preprint arXiv:1412.3661v4, Appendix A p. 15; retrieved 2026-09-02. The node follows by applying the quoted rectangular inequality to the centered 2p-vector (Z_1,...,Z_p,-Z_1,...,-Z_p), whose coordinate variances are one.

statements.statement:
Let \(m\geq2\), let \(Q_0,Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\) be probability measures on one measurable space with \(Q_j\ll Q_0\) for \(1\leq j\leq m\), and let \(\widehat J\) be any measurable map into \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).  Then
\[
 \frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m Q_j(\widehat J\neq j)
 \geq 1-\frac{m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)+\log2}{\log m}.
\]
The same inequality holds for randomized decoders after adjoining a randomization variable having one common law and independent of the observation under every \(Q_j\).

source.locator: Section 2.5, Lemma 2.10 (Fano's lemma) and its average-Kullback corollary
source.verbatim_statement: Lemma 2.10 (Fano’s lemma). Let P_0,P_1,...,P_M be probability measures on (X,A), M>=1. Then p_e,M <= M/(M+1) and g(p_e,M) >= log(M+1) - (M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=0}^M K(P_j,P), where P=(M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=0}^M P_j and g(x)=x log M+H(x). Equation (2.70): g(p_e,M) >= log(M+1) - (M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=1}^M K(P_j,P_0). Corollary 2.6: if (M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=1}^M K(P_j,P_0) <= alpha log M, then p_e,M >= [log(M+1)-log 2]/log M - alpha.

upstream.citation: Alexandre B. Tsybakov, Introduction to Nonparametric Estimation, Springer 2009, DOI 10.1007/978-0-387-79052-7
upstream.locator: Section 2.7.1, Lemma 2.10, equation (2.70), and Corollary 2.6, book pp. 111-115

attestation.note: Springer 2009 eBook ISBN 978-0-387-79052-7, lawfully accessed through the Ethiopian Statistical Service institutional repository, book pp. 111-115 (PDF pp. 120-124), retrieved 2026-09-02. The node is the usual uniform-prior decoder form: apply Lemma 2.10 to Q_1,...,Q_m and bound average KL to their mixture by average KL to the arbitrary reference Q_0; common independent auxiliary randomization leaves these KL values unchanged.

statements.statement:
Let \(n\geq4\), \(p\geq3\), and let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent centered vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\).  Suppose there are constants \(b>0\) and \(B_n\geq1\) such that
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E X_{ij}^2\geq b
 \quad\text{for every }j,
 \qquad
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E|X_{ij}|^{2+k}\leq B_n^k
 \quad\text{for every }j\text{ and }k\in\{1,2\},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\exp(|X_{ij}|/B_n)\leq2
 \quad\text{for every }i\text{ and }j.
\]
If \(S_n^X=n^{-1/2}\sum_iX_i\) and \(S_n^Y\) is centered Gaussian with the same covariance, then
\[
 \sup_{A\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}}|\mathbb P(S_n^X\in A)-\mathbb P(S_n^Y\in A)|
 \leq C_b\left\{\frac{B_n^2\log^7(pn)}n\right\}^{1/6}.
\]
If \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\) are independent standard Gaussians, independent of the vectors, \(\overline X=n^{-1}\sum_iX_i\), and \(\gamma\in(0,e^{-1})\), then, with probability at least \(1-\gamma\),
\[
 \sup_{A\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}}\left|
 \mathbb P\!\left\{n^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i(X_i-\overline X)\in A\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 -\mathbb P(S_n^Y\in A)\right|
 \leq C_b\left\{\frac{B_n^2\log^5(pn)\log^2(1/\gamma)}n\right\}^{1/6}.
\]

source.locator: Proposition 2.1 and conditions (M.1), (M.2), (E.1), p. 5; Section 4.1 and Corollary 4.2, pp. 9--12, author preprint arXiv:1412.3661v4
source.verbatim_statement: Suppose that conditions (M.1) and (M.2) are satisfied. Then under (E.1), we have \(\rho_n(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}})\leq C D_n^{(1)}\).

statements.statement:
For the independent row vectors with coordinates \(\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}(O_{n,i})/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\), unit coordinate variances, and standardized sub-exponential envelope \(\mathfrak E_n(P^{(n)})\), the condition
\[
 \left\{\mathfrak E_n(P^{(n)})^2\log^7(nK_n)/n\right\}^{1/6}\to0
\]
implies uniform Gaussian approximation for the maximum of the absolute standardized sums and conditional Gaussian-multiplier approximation based on their empirically centered values, with Gaussian covariance \(R_{P^{(n)}}\).

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2.1 (Abstract High Dimensional CLT for Hyperrectangles). Suppose that there exists some constant b > 0 such that n^{-1} sum_{i=1}^n E[X_{ij}^2] >= b for all j = 1,...,p. Then there exist constants K_1,K_2 > 0 depending only on b such that for every constant bar L_n >= L_n, rho_n(A^re) <= K_1[(bar L_n^2 log^7 p/n)^{1/6} + M_n(phi_n)/bar L_n], with phi_n := K_2(bar L_n^2 log^4 p/n)^{-1/6}. Corollary 4.2 (Multiplier Bootstrap for Hyperrectangles). Let alpha in (0,e^{-1}) be a constant, and suppose that conditions (M.1) and (M.2) are satisfied. Then under (E.1), with probability at least 1-alpha, rho_n^{MB}(A^re) <= C D_n^{(1)}(alpha), where C depends only on b.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\underline w\leq1/12\), \(|J_n|\geq2\) eventually, \(\delta_nK_n^3\to0\), and \(\sup_n\nu_nK_n\leq\bar\nu<\infty\).  Every likelihood in \(\texttt{def:positive-noise-geometric-fano-family}\) is normalized, positive on the common support, and preserves the treatment mechanism, conditional outcome laws, causal feature \(b(u)=u\), and oracle nuisance functions of \(P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm g}\subseteq\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\), with the codebook, curvature, cell-radius, margin, and denominator bounds of \(\texttt{thm:fano-membership}\).  Define
\[
 \Gamma_2(K,L)=\frac{144H_2(K,L)}{\sqrt{V_K^{(0)}V_L^{(0)}}}.
\]
Then \(\Gamma_2(K,K)=1\) and \(\sup_{K\ne L;\,K,L\geq8}\Gamma_2(K,L)\leq1/5\).  Uniformly over \(j\in J_n\),
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}\left|\frac{\sigma_{P_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)},K}}
 {\sigma_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}}-1\right|
 +\sup_{K,L<K_n}\left|R_{P_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)}}(K,L)
 -R_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\right|
 \leq C_{\bar\nu}\delta_nK_n^2=o(1),
\]
and
\[
 G_{P_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(K)
 =-\delta_n\sqrt{V_K^{(0)}}\,\Gamma_2(K,j)
 +O_{\bar\nu}\!\left(\delta_n^2K_n^2\sigma_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}\right).
\]
There is \(a_{\bar\nu}>0\) such that
\[
 \min_{j\ne\ell;\,j,\ell\in J_n}\max_{K\in J_n}
 \frac{|G_{P_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_{\ell,\mathrm g}^{(n)}}(K)|}
 {\sigma_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}}
 \geq a_{\bar\nu}\delta_n,
\]
and \(\operatorname{KL}\{(P_{j,\mathrm g}^{(n)})^{\otimes n},(P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)})^{\otimes n}\}\leq Cn\delta_n^2\).
statements.justification: The geometric component remains a uniformly nonvanishing fraction of each adjacent influence score when \(\nu_nK_n=O(1)\), so a \(U\)-only likelihood tilt extends the information-theoretic packing to positive outcome noise without changing conditional outcome laws.
statements.gap: The noiseless full-score tilt does not by itself certify a common-support positive-noise observed-data packing, and the fixed-resolution causal clustering results do not provide one.
statements.consumer: This packing certifies the positive-noise converse used to limit fine MineThatData resolution reports; it is not an upper-band theorem.

statements.justification: The positive-noise geometric packing and the randomized Fano decoder force the same standardized simultaneous lower radius whenever \(\nu_nK_n=O(1)\).
statements.gap: No existing fixed-resolution result transfers an adjacent-score packing into a growing-resolution causal-band lower bound with positive residual variance.
statements.consumer: The result supplies a converse-only warning for MineThatData analyses with small but positive outcome noise.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\underline w\leq1/12\), \(\nu_n>0\), \(|J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}|\geq2\) eventually, \(\inf_n\nu_nK_n\geq\underline\nu\) for some fixed \(\underline\nu>0\), \(\nu_n\delta_n=O(r_n)\), and \(\delta_nK_n^5\to0\).  Then every law in \(\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm r}\) is normalized, positive on the common observed support, and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), belongs to \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\).  Under \(P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)}\),
\[
 e_j(u)=1/2,qquad
 b_j(u)=u-\nu_n\tanh\!\left\{\frac{24\delta_nF_{j}^{\mathrm r}(u)}{\sqrt{A_j}}\right\}.
\]
Uniformly over \(j\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}\) and \(K\leq K_n\), its codebooks are unique and interior,
\[
 \|C_{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)},K}-C_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}\|_2
 \leq C\{\delta_nK^3\}^{1/2},\quad
 \lambda_{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)},K}\geq cK^{-3},\quad
 s_{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)},K}\asymp K^{-1},
\]
and one may take \(\kappa=c/K\), margin exponent one, and a uniformly bounded margin coefficient.  Furthermore,
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}\left|\frac{\sigma_{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)},K}}
 {\sigma_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}}-1\right|
 +\sup_{K,L<K_n}\left|R_{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)}}(K,L)
 -R_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\right|
 \leq C_{\underline\nu}\{\delta_nK_n^5\}^{1/2}=o(1).
\]
The pathwise gain derivative in the pure residual direction is
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{dt}G_{P_{t,j}^{\mathrm{pure\ r}}}(K)\right|_{t=0}
 =-\nu_n\sqrt{A_K}\,\Gamma_1(K,j),
\]
where \(dP_{t,j}^{\mathrm{pure\ r}}/dP_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\) is proportional to \(\exp(-t\gamma_{n,j}^{\mathrm r})\).  For the denominator-reinforced hybrid family and \(K,j\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}\),
\[
 G_{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(K)
 =-\delta_n\!\left\{\nu_n\sqrt{A_K}\,\Gamma_1(K,j)
 +a_{\mathrm h}\sqrt{V_K^{(0)}}\,\Gamma_2(K,j)\right\}
 +O_{\underline\nu}\!\left(\delta_n\sigma_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}
 \{\delta_nK_n^5\}^{1/2}\right).
\]
There is \(a_{\underline\nu}>0\) such that
\[
 \min_{j\ne\ell;\,j,\ell\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}}\max_{K\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}}
 \frac{|G_{P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_{\ell,\mathrm r}^{(n)}}(K)|}
 {\sigma_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}}
 \geq a_{\underline\nu}\delta_n,
\]
and \(\operatorname{KL}\{(P_{j,\mathrm r}^{(n)})^{\otimes n},(P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)})^{\otimes n}\}\leq Cn\delta_n^2\).

For every \(\nu_n>0\) and \(K,L\geq8\), the uniform residual directions satisfy
\[
 E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}\gamma_{n,K}^{\mathrm r}=0,\qquad
 E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(\gamma_{n,K}^{\mathrm r})^2=1,
 \qquad \sup_{K\geq8}\|\gamma_{n,K}^{\mathrm r}\|_\infty<\infty,
\]
and
\[
 E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(\gamma_{n,K}^{\mathrm r}\gamma_{n,L}^{\mathrm r})
 =\Gamma_1(K,L).
\]
Moreover \(\Gamma_1(K,K)=1\) and \(\sup_{K\ne L;\,K,L\geq8}\Gamma_1(K,L)\leq7/25\).

Suppose \(\underline w\leq1/12\), \(\inf_n\nu_nK_n\geq\underline\nu\) for some fixed \(\underline\nu>0\), \(\nu_n\delta_n=O(r_n)\), and \(\delta_nK_n^5\to0\).  Let \(B_n\) be any common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable rectangular-band procedure for which there is a deterministic \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}}
 \mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\!\left\{G_{P^{(n)}}(K)\in[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]
 \text{ for every }1\leq K<K_n\right\}\geq1-\alpha-\eta_n.
\]
Then there are constants \(c_{0,\underline\nu},c_{1,\underline\nu}>0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\), some \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_{n,\mathrm r}\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\!\left\{
 \max_{K\in J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}}\frac{\sqrt n\,h_{n,K}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 \geq c_{0,\underline\nu}\sqrt{\log|J_n^{\mathrm{hi}}|}\right\}
 \geq c_{1,\underline\nu}.
\]
This is a full-class lower-transfer result only.

Suppose \(\underline w\leq1/12\),
\[
 \mathbf1\{\nu_nK_n\leq1\}\delta_nK_n^3
 +\mathbf1\{\nu_nK_n>1\}\delta_nK_n^5\to0,
 \qquad
 \mathbf1\{\nu_nK_n>1\}\nu_n\delta_n=O(r_n).
\]
Let \((\mathcal U_n^\star,I_n^\star)\) be the rowwise piecewise experiment in \(\texttt{def:piecewise-all-noise-experiment}\).  Let \(B_n\) be any common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable rectangular-band procedure for which there is a deterministic \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}}
 \mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\!\left\{G_{P^{(n)}}(K)\in[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]
 \text{ for every }1\leq K<K_n\right\}\geq1-\alpha-\eta_n.
\]
Then there are universal constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\), some \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n^\star\subseteq\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\!\left\{
 \max_{K\in I_n^\star}\frac{\sqrt n\,h_{n,K}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 \geq c_0\sqrt{\log K_n}\right\}\geq c_1.
\]
Thus positive outcome noise at any scale does not remove the \(\sqrt{\log K_n/n}\) standardized simultaneous lower radius under the stated rowwise localization and nuisance-envelope conditions.  This theorem asserts neither a feasible positive-noise upper band nor matching outside the noiseless local experiment.

sampling_model.design: Observational or randomized binary-treatment rows satisfying consistency, conditional exchangeability, and overlap; the exact lower-bound witness is a randomized trial.
sampling_model.units: For each row \(n\), \(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are independent draws from \(P^{(n)}\).
sampling_model.overlap: A fixed \(\epsilon\)-overlap condition is imposed, and fitted propensities are clipped by construction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted propensity and outcome-regression learners attain the primitive rate \(r_n\); codebooks are reoptimized separately at every resolution.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published Abstract, lines 134--163, reports plug-in estimation and bias-corrected semiparametric root-\(n\) inference with asymptotic normality for causal \(k\)-means targets.
Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.2, Proposition 3.1 on PDF pages 10--12 give a margin-dependent fixed-resolution excess-distortion upper bound and a fixed-\(k\) minimax lower bound.

The title page and Abstract on page 3643 state simultaneous confidence regions for many functional parameters using approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores and high-dimensional uniform central limit theory.
Preprint Theorem 2.1 gives Gaussian approximation for hyperrectangles, and Section 4 gives multiplier-bootstrap approximation for maxima of supplied high-dimensional sums.
The manuscript sharpens Gaussian and bootstrap approximation rates for nondegenerate high-dimensional covariance structures.
The article derives lower bounds for the length of honest adaptive nonparametric confidence intervals.
The paper studies plug-in hierarchical linkages and density level sets of vector counterfactual features.

Abstract p. 1 and Introduction pp. 3–4 study convergence of optimal K-level quantizers and distortion performance for Wasserstein-convergent probability-measure sequences, including empirical measures, with bounds depending on the quantization level.

tldr: Adjacent causal-clustering resolutions share reoptimized codebooks and highly structured noise, so their joint inferential price is determined by the covariance geometry of their efficient scores rather than by the number of reported resolutions alone. The proposal computes the full uniform-law covariance through periodic Bernoulli polynomials and greatest-common-divisor identities, proves that the resulting process contains a linearly growing separated packing, derives a corrected cross-fitted band with intrinsic Gaussian-width radius, and matches it over the explicit local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\) with a genuine multi-resolution Fano lower bound whose tilted observed-data laws remain in one nondegenerate quantizer neighborhood.

project_justification.gap: Fixed-resolution causal \(k\)-means inference and quantizer geometry do not determine the covariance-aware minimax price of reporting an entire adjacent causal-distortion process. LiuPages2020 overlaps the optimizer- and distortion-performance-stability ingredient at fixed or level-by-level quantization, but its verified scope does not provide uniform \(K\le K_n\) control at shrinking adjacent-score scales, causal nuisance correction, joint adjacent efficient-score covariance, multiplier calibration, or a multi-resolution causal Fano lower bound. High-dimensional bootstrap theory treats supplied score arrays rather than this optimized causal process.
project_justification.niche: The exact cross-resolution kernel creates a theorem-level route to distinguish an intrinsic joint penalty from a crude coordinate-count penalty and to certify that penalty by a causal observed-data packing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the arithmetic covariance and semimetric, controls optimized-risk and nuisance remainders at the associated Gaussian width, and proves matching upper and Fano lower bounds over the explicit local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\), while retaining only uniform linearization over the broader causal-quantizer class.
